definitions.explanation: Having or displaying a commanding, awe-inspiring, and dignified presence. A four-character idiom ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) describing someone or something that exudes authority and magnificence.

examples.japanese: {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}と{歩|ある}く。
examples.english: To walk with dignity and grandeur.

examples.japanese: {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}とした{態度|たいど}で{演説|えんぜつ}した。
examples.english: He gave the speech with an imposing demeanor.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}は{威風堂々|いふうどうどう}たる{姿|すがた}で{山|やま}の{上|うえ}にそびえている。
examples.english: The castle stands majestically atop the mountain.

notes:
A {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} (four-character idiom) composed of {威風|いふう} (dignified air, majesty) + {堂々|どうどう} (grand, imposing). Describes a powerful, awe-inspiring presence.

ETYMOLOGY:
{威|い} (authority) + {風|ふう} (manner) + {堂|どう} (stately) + {堂|どう} (stately) — "an authoritative manner, grandly stately."

USAGE:
- As an adverb: {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}と + verb
- As a modifier: {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}とした + noun / {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}たる + noun

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}と{構|かま}える: to assume a dignified stance
- {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}とした{姿|すがた}: a majestic figure
- {威風堂々|いふうどうどう}たる{態度|たいど}: an imposing attitude

CULTURAL NOTE:
Also the Japanese title of Edward Elgar's famous march "Pomp and Circumstance" ({威風堂々|いふうどうどう}), well known in Japan as a graduation ceremony piece.
